jobs.title: NSA 2027 Future Computing Summer Internship (FCSI) - APPLICATION DEADLINE OCT 31, 2026, at 11:59PM EST at Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education
jobs.description: Employer: Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education Expires: 10/24/2026 The Laboratory for Physical Sciences (LPS) Advanced Computing Systems (ACS) team in the NSA Research Directorate is joining its counterparts in the Capabilities and Operations Directorates to provide a select number of undergraduate students with an exciting 10-week summer internship at LPS, located in the Research Park building complex adjacent to the University of Maryland, Baltimore County (UMBC). The Future Computing Summer Internship (FCSI) program was established in 2022 to expose participants to High-Performance Computing (HPC), a field critical to national security, discovery, and technological innovation. FCSI is intended for undergraduate students who will complete their junior year by Spring 2027 and are pursuing degrees in Mathematics, Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Physics, or Artificial Intelligence. These students possess strong mathematical and computer programming foundations and technical skills relevant to HPC. What will I be doing?As a selected participant, you will collaborate with a team led by NSA researchers in HPC to solve future computing problems relevant to the NSA Mission. Under the mentorship of technical researchers, you will gain skills in a variety of areas relevant to HPC. Why should I apply?The projects involve hands-on technical research activities spanning disciplines and include, but are not limited to:HPC file transfer and parallel programming, among others.BenchmarkingComputational physicsArtificial IntelligenceAt the end of the internship, you will have the opportunity to present the results of your research to an audience that includes multiple accomplished researchers in each project area, NSA seniors, and members of internal NSA engineering/computer science/math communities. **Application Deadline: 10/31/2026 11:59:00 PM Eastern Time Zone**Where will I be located?Catonsville, MarylandWhat is the anticipated start date?The National Security Agency (NSA) is making selections for the program, which is scheduled to begin Monday, June 7, 2027, and conclude Friday, August 13, 2027. Applicants eligible for lodging will be able to check into the lodging facility on Sunday, 6 June 2027 and will check out of the lodging facility on Saturday, 14 August 2027.What is the appointment length?This appointment is a ten-week, full-time summer research appointment.What are the provisions?$1,000.00 per week stipend. Stipend payments are issued monthly and will be deposited on the last business day of each month.Travel and housing will be provided to eligible participants whose permanent residence is located more than 50 miles from the facility.Other financial support provisions will be determined based on individual participant situational needs.About ORISEThis program, administered by Oak Ridge Associated Universities (ORAU) through its contract with the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) to manage the Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education (ORISE), was established through an interagency agreement between DOE and DoD. Participants do not enter an employee/employer relationship with ORISE, ORAU, DoD, or any other office or agency. Instead, you will be affiliated with ORISE for the administration of the appointment through the ORISE appointment letter and Terms of Appointment. Proof of health insurance is required for participation in this program. Health insurance can be obtained through ORISE. For more information, visit the ORISE Research Participation Program at the U.S. Department of Defense.Qualifications The qualified candidate will be enrolled full-time as an undergraduate student at an accredited U.S. institution at the time of applying. This internship opportunity is intended for undergraduates graduating in December of 2027 or Spring of 2028 who have completed significant upper-level coursework/experience in math, computer science, computer engineering, or related STEM fields. **Application Deadline: 10/31/2026 11:59:00 PM Eastern Time Zone**Application RequirementsZintellect ProfileEducational and Employment HistoryEssay Questions (goals, experiences, and skills relevant to the opportunity)Resume (PDF)Transcripts/Academic Records - please upload a copy of a transcript for your current or most recent degree program that meets the disciplinary qualifications of the opportunity. One letter of recommendation from a mentor highlighting your qualifications and how you will be successful during an internship focused on HPC. We encourage you to contact your recommender(s) as soon as you start the application process to ensure they are able to complete the recommendation form and to let them know to expect a message from Zintellect. Recommenders will be asked to rate your scientific capabilities, personal characteristics, and describe how they know you. You can always log back in to your Zintellect account and check the status of your application. **Recommendations must be submitted by your recommender(s) no later than the application closing date. Applications without the required recommendations by the deadline will not be reviewed or considered for selection.**If you have questions, send an email to STEM-WORKFORCE@orise.orau.gov. Please list the reference code of this opportunity [NSA-2026-0001] in the subject line of the email. Please understand that ORISE does not review applications or select applicants; selections are made by the sponsoring agency identified on this opportunity. All application materials should be submitted via the “Apply” button at the bottom of this opportunity listing. Please do not send application materials to the email address above.Connect with ORISE...on the GO! Download the new ORISE GO mobile app in the Apple App Store or Google Play Store to help you stay engaged, connected, and informed during your ORISE experience and beyond!

jobs.title: Manufacturing Technician at Cytrellis Biosystems
jobs.description: Employer: Cytrellis Biosystems Expires: 10/24/2026 The Manufacturing Technician is a hands-on position within manufacturing where you’ll be a vital part of the team’s execution of Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) activities on the manufacturing floor. You’ll perform functions associated with GMP manufacturing operations including but not limited to assembly, testing, lot and serial management, material controls, process adherence, and maintaining a clean and hygienic manufacturing area. A successful candidate will have a strong mechanical aptitude, specifically with smaller detailed assemblies requiring a strong attention to detail. Please note, due to a new product this is a temp. role until we define a CMO, we anticipate the role will be 3-6 month assignment. You must be able to come on site 5 days a week to the Woburn MA office and have work authorization. Essential Duties and Responsibilities: Assembly and testing of the Cytrellis ellacor system including the main console and hand piece. Responsible for meeting production demands within the work cell. Responsible for ensuring that final products meet quality objectives and specifications. Responsible for accurate recording keeping when assembling, inspecting, and repairing products or materials. Work alongside quality with investigation of non-conformances. Technical support on equipment and processes with respect to process yields, equipment OEE, TPM and health and safety. Work with manufacturing engineering to develop and troubleshoot processes and procedures. Assist in the creation and maintenance of work instructions and documentation in area of responsibility. Assist in root cause analysis and implement corrective actions. Adhere to quality and compliance standards to ensure safe and effective use of equipment and tools in the manufacturing of medical devices. Ability to establish and maintain working relationships cross functionally including production, QA, QC, engineering, validation, and maintenance. Overtime hours may be required to meet customer demand. Other duties as assigned. Education and/or Experience: A high school diploma. Two-year technical degree or equivalent experience. Skilled in complex electromechanical assembly. Skilled in the safe handling of Printed Circuit boards and electronic components. Ability to solder and use basic electronic test equipment. Experience reviewing Medical Device, Device History Records (DHR) strongly preferred. Must be able to problem-solve independently and when working as a team. Ability to assemble complex assemblies requiring a high level of accuracy and precision. Strong mechanical aptitude, specifically with smaller detailed assemblies requiring a strong attention to detail. Understand the appropriate use of fasteners, torque wrenches, thread lock and other bonding agents. Ability to read work instructions, schematics, assembly drawings, and prints. Basic computer skills required. Experience in metrology techniques a plus. Physical Requirements: Prolonged periods of sitting at a desk and working on a computer. Must be able to lift 15 pounds at times. Utilize a variety of handheld tools. Normal color vision or ability to recognize cable colors correctly. Limited Local travel may be needed on occasion.

We take pride in creating a culture where our people are valued, supported, and provided opportunities for growth and belonging. By joining Southern Glazer’s, you would be part of a team that values excellence, innovation, and community. This is more than just a job – it's an opportunity to build the future of beverage distribution and grow with a company that truly cares about its people. Southern Glazer’s offers a competitive compensation package with an hourly pay rate of $25 / hour. In determining a final offer, the company will evaluate a specific candidate's education, skills and experience and will make an offer appropriately. OverviewThe Southern Glazer’s Internship Program was established to develop the next generation of Technology leaders. Each summer, the program offers interns the opportunity to engage in career building activities while simultaneously learning and applying industry-leading practices.This hands-on experience gives interns the chance to explore and understand the adult beverage industry. The knowledge gained from industry leaders will allow you to build a network of professionals within the beverage alcohol industry and here at Southern Glazer’s. Being a Southern Glazer’s intern means you’ll be invited to our Leadership Spotlight Series, a Community Service Day exclusive to our intern class, as well as access to Professional Development workshops and trainings!Primary ResponsibilitiesAs a OneTech Intern, you’ll work in a variety of Digital and Technology areas, including but not limited to: Enterprise Products & Platforms, Data & Analytics, Infrastructure & Ops, Cybersecurity, and Digital Strategy, to gain knowledge and understanding of technology’s role in the wine and spirits distribution industry. This role will be specifically working with the QA team, learning and building skills in software test automation including development and maintenance of automated test scripts, executing manual and automated test cases, automation testing best practices, improving test coverage and test efficiency, etc. The structured internship is designed to expose students to the wine and spirits Three-Tier beverage distribution system and the role technology plays to enable business capabilities. Interns will finish the program having gained broad experience in various aspects of the relationship between technology, sales and operations. Part of the experience will include supporting projects as assigned and defined by student’s specific learning goals, participating in training, on-site meetings, and department wide learning opportunities as available. Lastly, interns will complete an end of internship project showcasing one’s knowledge and present to management. jobs.description: Employer: Haworth Expires: 10/24/2026 Job Title: Design Research InternCompany OverviewAt Haworth, we're not just creating office furniture; we're shaping dynamic workspaces. jobs.description: Employer: Cleveland-Cliffs Expires: 10/24/2026 Cleveland-Cliffs takes pride in offering a variety of opportunities for students and new graduates who have an interest in the steel industry and a passion for innovation and sustainability. We offer a best-in-class internship program in the industry and partner with many universities to provide co-op opportunities. Working beside industry-leading engineering and operational leaders, our interns/co-ops will create meaningful solutions to real-world problems. As an intern/co-op with Cleveland-Cliffs, you will build life-long professional connections and have the opportunity to be considered for future full-time employment. As a Health & Safety Intern, the projects assigned will vary based on the intern’s education level and plant location, but will generally reflect the duties outlined below. jobs.description: Employer: Nimo Technology Inc. Expires: 10/25/2026 Nimo Robotics — Mechanical Engineering Intern JDJob Title: Mechanical Engineering Intern — Dexterous Hand & End-Effector Design Location: Mountain View, CA — On-site Employment Type: Internship — immediate start, with an intern-to-full-time conversion track Pay: $35 per hour (negotiable based on experience)About Nimo Robotics Nimo Robotics is building next-generation humanoid systems — including dexterous robotic hands and end-effectors — capable of human-level manipulation. Founded by a team of Stanford PhD alumni, we have already signed letters of intent with leading U.S. enterprise customers and are growing our engineering team to deliver.About the Role We're hiring Mechanical Engineering Interns to work at the intersection of hardware and software on the heart of our humanoid system: dexterous hands and end-effectors. This is not a shadowing internship — you'll own real design work from concept and CAD through prototyping, testing, and iteration, working directly with our founding team. The internship is designed as a pipeline to full-time: strong performers will be considered for a full-time offer at the end of the program.What You'll DoDesign mechanisms and components for dexterous robotic hands and end-effectors — fingers, joints, linkages, and tendon/cable-driven transmissionsOwn mechatronics design: motor selection and sizing, actuator packaging, and sensor/electronics integrationOwn parts end to end: CAD design, rapid prototyping (3D printing, machining), assembly, and functional testingRun tolerance analysis and DFM reviews, and iterate quickly based on test resultsParticipate in full-system testing of the robot — integration, bring-up, validation, and debugging alongside our software and controls engineersCreate and maintain engineering drawings, BOMs, and test documentationCandidates with controls experience will also have the opportunity to take on robot operation work — motor/force control tuning, teleoperation, and hardware-in-the-loop testing.Minimum QualificationsCurrently pursuing a BS or MS in Mechanical Engineering, Robotics, Mechatronics, or a related fieldStrong CAD skills (SolidWorks or equivalent)Solid fundamentals in mechanism design, machine elements, and materialsDemonstrated hands-on engineering experience through a prior internship or co-op, a project team (e.g., Formula SAE, robotics club), or a research lab — you've designed, built, and debugged real hardwarePreferred QualificationsExperience designing robotic hands, grippers, end-effectors, or other precision electromechanical mechanismsFamiliarity with tendon/cable-driven or linkage-driven mechanisms, small actuators, and gear/transmission designControls experience: motor control, force/torque control, or teleoperationProgramming skills (Python or C++); ROS experience is a plusFamiliarity with GD&T, FEA, and common manufacturing processesDetailsStart date: as soon as possible; duration is flexible, with the intent to convert to a full-time roleSchedule: full-time preferred; part-time (20+ hrs/week) considered for current studentsIntern-to-full-time track: we hire interns with the intention of converting top performers to full-time rolesWork authorization: F-1 international students eligible for CPT or OPT are welcome to applyNimo Robotics is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applicants of all backgrounds.

jobs.title: Content Marketing Intern (20-40hrs/week) at EF Education First
jobs.description: Employer: EF Education First Expires: 10/28/2026 About the role At EF Ultimate Break, we inspire 18–35-year-olds to join life-changing travel experiences around the world. Our travelers include college students escaping campus to bop around Europe, young professionals who’ve stockpiled PTO taking their dream trip to Japan, and everyone in between. We’re looking for a college student or recent grad with a sharp eye for digital-first creative, cultural moments, and emerging trends. Someone who can translate ideas into work that earns the attention of the next generation of travelers. From TikTok ads and CMS updates to trip launches and organizing swag for teams. you’ll have the opportunity to work on a wide range of projects that directly influence how travelers discover and experience our brand.Consider this a professional outlet for your travel obsession.This is a cross-functional role built for someone who’s organized, curious, people-oriented, and genuinely excited about how content works across channels, across teams, and across formats. This role is ideal for someone who enjoys variety and is excited to jump between hands-on tasks—from making site updates and creating graphics to QAing content and supporting day-to-day marketing projects.You’ll partner with our Growth and Creative teams to bring content to life: building landing pages, making updates in our CMS, creating and optimizing digital ads, and ensuring our brand shows up as its best across channels. You don’t need to be an expert in all of it on day one, but you do need the drive to learn fast and the people skills to work across teams. What you’ll do -Source, organize, and create content in our CMS for the Ultimate Break website, ranging from promotional graphics to content-rich landing pages and itinerary pages -Create compelling content for paid media advertising and work with the team to optimize and refine ads for stronger performance -Support content calendars, asset libraries, and documentation for your projects so nothing falls through the cracks -Leverage agentic tools to automate repetitive production tasks: generating copy variations for landing pages, adapting email content for different segments, etc.What we’re looking for Required -Some experience in content creation and comfort with learning new systems -A keen eye for design and copy to ensure consistency of our branded content across channels -A natural communicator who’s comfortable working with different teams -A hands-on comfort with AI tools; you’ve used AI agents to get work done faster, without losing sight of taste, originality, and craft. -Excellent organizational skills and attention to detail -Strong verbal and visual communication skills with the ability to interpret direction -An interest in keeping up with (and sharing!) evolving Gen Z and Millennial trendsAdditional helpful (but not mandatory) skills: Experience working with a CMS and ad platforms -Experience working with an ecommerce/DTC brand -Some knowledge of Figma and Canva -Light video, animation, or motion skillsWhy this role You’ll get visibility across nearly every marketing function: ecommerce, paid media, CRM, and branded content. We’re a team that moves fast, values good ideas and is actively investing in how AI agents can power our workflows. The practical stuff—and why it’s part of the fun• $25 per hour: This is a paid, hourly internship.• 20–40 hours per week: We’re open to interns who can contribute anywhere from 20 to 40 hours each week. Whether you’re a student with 20 hours available or a recent graduate looking for full-time hours, we’ll work together to find a schedule that fits.• On-site collaboration: During your working hours, you’ll work from the office alongside our creative and marketing teams. We believe the best ideas often come from being in the room together—sharing feedback, brainstorming, and learning from one another. About UsSome companies are in the business of banking. Others are in the business of shoes. Or sports. Or soft drinks. At EF, we're in a different kind of business. One that's a little less tangible, and a lot more important. Because our business, what we make, makes everything else possible. We're in the business of understanding. Between people. Between cultures.For over half a century we’ve been the leader in international educational programs and experiences designed to foster such understanding. Through language, cultural exchange, academic studies, and educational travel, we create the kinds of immersive experiences that challenge biases, open minds, and pave the way for a more understanding world. You’ll find our offices and schools located in some of the world’s greatest cities, and filled with smart, driven people (over 50,000 of us) who push each other to be better every day. But it’s what we do together - building greater understanding, breaking down barriers, and creating a better world - that makes all the difference. Founded in 1965 in Sweden, EF (Education First) is a global association of education companies that share a common mission of opening the world through education. EF has been recognized on Forbes 2025 and 2024 World’s Best Employers and 2024 Top Companies for Women lists, Fast Company’s 2025 Next Big Things In Tech, and was a 2024 App Store Award winner in Cultural Impact. About the TeamAt EF Ultimate Break, we’re about way more than collecting passport stamps. Our guided tours empower young adults aged 18–35 to explore a world outside their comfort zones. Each immersive tour creates experiences that last a lifetime, building bonds with fellow travelers that go beyond borders and cultures, and help bring the world a little bit closer. WARNING: Working at Ultimate Break may inspire your own desire to experience the world, good news is- we’ll help with that! Learn more about EF Ultimate Break: https://www.efultimatebreak.com/

jobs.title: Field/Office Engineer Intern (California High Speed Rail Program) at Luster National, Inc.
jobs.description: Employer: Luster National, Inc. Expires: 10/28/2026 About the Position Our 2027 Internship Program offers a 10-week immersive experience, providing in-depth training in Oracle Primavera P6 scheduling, plan and contract reviews, as well as practical field engineering tasks, including structural inspections of California High-Speed Rail (CA HSR) bridges under construction. As a Luster Intern, you will gain hands-on experience in key project delivery functions such as quantity take-offs, quality control inspections, and change order tracking. Intern Program participants include Luster (Employer of Interns), AECOM/Fluor JV (Prime Consulting Firms that Luster works with on the Project), and California High Speed Rail Authority (Client of AECOM/Fluor JV).We are hiring two Interns majoring in Civil Engineering or Construction Management to join our team. Interns will collaborate closely with experienced Luster Engineers at CA HSR and have the opportunity to engage with representatives from Luster, AECOM/Fluor, and CA HSR. These engagements may include breakfast or lunch meetings, social events, and scheduled meetings, providing interns with valuable insights into the program’s organization and management. Interns will actively engage in team meetings, project site visits, safety training, and special project events. Every effort will be made to fully integrate Interns as valued members of the infrastructure delivery team. This internship provides a unique opportunity to acquire valuable industry experience and develop essential skills in a dynamic, supportive environment.As one of our Field/Office Engineer Interns, you will develop critical skills in construction management by learning how our team oversees contractor activities related to cost, schedule, and budget. You will gain hands-on experience in essential project management areas such as scheduling, estimating, and monitoring construction progress. This role offers a balanced combination of fieldwork and office tasks, allowing you to track and manage construction activities effectively.Your responsibilities will include conducting design reviews for field construction, performing quantity estimations, carrying out field inspections, and assessing schedules for potential delays. Additionally, you will participate in executive and team meetings, providing you with valuable insight into the complex, dynamic elements that drive successful project delivery. Key Responsibilities Project Oversight & Monitoring: Shadow and support our Project Manager in applying strategies and tools for verifying design and construction processes. You’ll assist in tracking, measuring, and reporting on essential project metrics like scope, quality, risk, schedule, and cost.Contractor Coordination: Learn about the methods and techniques our construction management team uses to oversee contractor activities, focusing on budget, schedule, and cost controls.Scope Development & Estimation: Contribute to the development of scope of work and level of effort assessments, and gain exposure to the critical aspects of scheduling and estimating in project management.Field & Office Work: Your responsibilities will include both on-site fieldwork (transportation with the Luster Intern Mentor) and office-based tasks related to tracking and managing construction activities, giving you a well-rounded view of project management.Design & Construction Review: Take part in design reviews, quantity estimations, field inspections, and schedule evaluations. You’ll also analyze potential delay impacts and learn how to address them.Executive Exposure: Attend executive meetings and participate in team discussions, project site walks, safety training, and special events to gain a comprehensive understanding of how large infrastructure projects are managed.Minimum Qualifications The program is open to undergraduate students (Junior or Senior level) enrolled in Civil Engineering or Construction Management, or a related major at an accredited four-year university in California, such as California State University, Fresno (‘Fresno State’) or University of California, Merced (‘UC Merced’). Eligible applicants should have completed at least two years of coursework toward their degree. The program is particularly well-suited for Juniors and Seniors who have made significant progress in completing their core degree requirements.Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (e.g., Word, Excel, PowerPoint).Willingness to travel to field sites as needed.What’s In It for You Hands-On Experience: Gain practical exposure to a major infrastructure project with the California High-Speed Rail, working directly on real-world construction management activities.Skill Building: Develop essential skills in project management, including scheduling, estimating, design review, and field inspection, while learning how to track key project metrics like quality, risk, and cost.Professional Mentorship: Work side-by-side with an experienced Project Manager who will guide you through the complexities of managing large-scale construction projects, offering insights and industry knowledge.Diverse Learning Opportunities: Balance your time between fieldwork and office tasks, giving you a well-rounded experience that covers both on-the-ground construction activities and the strategic aspects of project oversight.Networking and Exposure: Attend executive and team meetings, participate in project site walks, and join safety training and special events, providing you with networking opportunities and a deeper understanding of project delivery.Career Preparation: This internship offers a solid foundation for your future career, enhancing your resume with hands-on experience in one of the nation’s most ambitious rail projects.Impactful Work Experience: Be part of a transformative project that’s shaping the future of transportation in California, giving you a chance to make a real impact and contribute to the success of a high-profile public infrastructure initiative.Salary The interns will be W-2 employees of Luster and will be paid $20/hr. Internship Dates The duration of the Luster National, Inc. Internship Program is 10 weeks with a schedule of Monday through Friday from 8am to 5pm PT. Start Date: Tuesday, June 1, 2027End Date: Friday, August 6, 2027 Application Procedures Candidates should prepare a resume to submit with their application that includes past work experience; engineering and related coursework; computer and technology skills/expertise; and a brief statement of why they are interested in our internship program. Deadline Applications should be submitted no later than Friday, October 30, 2026. Interview Process The Luster team will conduct interviews with candidates and extend offers to finalists by late-November 2026 for the June 2027 cohort.

jobs.title: LVDT/RVDT Engineering Intern at RAM Aerospace
jobs.description: Employer: RAM Aerospace Expires: 10/28/2026 RAM Aerospace is a leader in aerospace innovation, powering flight and space exploration with precision solenoids, valves, actuators, and position sensing solutions. Since 1975, we've supported missions like the Space Shuttle and continue to deliver mission-critical components for commercial, defense, and satellite systems. Headquartered in St. George, Utah, our advanced manufacturing facility produces the precision solenoids, valves, and actuators that aerospace programs worldwide depend on. Our Valencia facility extends that capability with specialized manufacturing of LVDTs and RVDTs, critical position sensing devices used across a broad range of aerospace and defense applications. As one of Southern Utah's largest employers, we drive economic growth and offer high-skilled careers in engineering and manufacturing. From both facilities, we build the future of aerospace—on time, with excellence, and as a team. Join us to work on groundbreaking technology and help shape the future of flight and space exploration. Your career takes off here!RAM Aerospace's LVDT/RVDT Intern program is built for engineering students who want more than a summer project. This is a year-round, part-time position designed to fit alongside your academic schedule, giving you sustained, meaningful exposure to the design, analysis, test, and manufacturing of Linear Variable Differential Transformers, the precision position sensing devices that aerospace and defense systems worldwide depend on. You will work directly alongside experienced engineers and technicians, contributing to real work on real hardware across multiple disciplines. By the time you finish school, you will have built a level of hands-on aerospace engineering experience that very few of your peers can match. If you are an engineering student who is eager to learn, ready to contribute, and looking for a role that grows with you through your academic career, this opportunity was built for you.Duties and ResponsibilitiesDesign & Engineering Support: Assist RAM engineers in the design and development of LVDT/RVDT components and assemblies. Support CAD modeling, drawing updates, and design documentation using 3D CAD tools, and contribute to design reviews and engineering analysis tasks as your skills and familiarity with the product grow over time.Analysis & Performance Modeling: Support engineering analysis efforts related to LVDT/RVDT performance, including electromagnetic behavior, dimensional tolerance reviews, and basic mechanical assessments. Learn to apply analytical tools and methods under the guidance of senior engineers, building a working understanding of how design decisions translate into measurable performance outcomes.Test Support & Data Collection: Assist in the setup, execution, and documentation of LVDT/RVDT performance and functional testing. Operate test equipment under supervision, collect and log test data accurately, and support the analysis and reporting of test results in a format that informs engineering decisions.Manufacturing & Assembly Support: Work alongside technicians in the assembly of LVDT/RVDT components and subassemblies, learning proper assembly techniques, workmanship standards, and the attention to detail that precision aerospace hardware demands. Support manufacturing operations in a manner that reinforces RAM's quality and FOD prevention standards at all times.Documentation & Continuous Learning: Maintain accurate records of engineering and assembly activities in accordance with RAM's quality management system requirements. Engage actively with the engineers and technicians around you, ask good questions, take ownership of your development, and bring growing capability and initiative to your work with each passing semester.RequirementsLegal: Must be able to pass a comprehensive criminal background check and drug screening.ITAR: Must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum (due to ITAR requirements).Currently enrolled in a Bachelor's degree program in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or a closely related field required.Minimum sophomore standing required. Junior or senior standing preferred.Basic understanding of electromagnetic or electromechanical principles gained through coursework is a plus.Exposure to 3D CAD software through coursework or personal projects preferred. SolidWorks experience a plus.Ability to read and interpret basic engineering drawings and written assembly procedures.Strong attention to detail and genuine commitment to accuracy in both hands-on work and documentation.Ability to commit to a consistent part-time schedule throughout the academic year, with flexibility to increase hours during breaks if desired.Eager to learn, self-motivated, and comfortable working in an active manufacturing and engineering environment alongside experienced professionals.Clear written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to document work accurately and collaborate effectively with engineers and technicians.We are committed to creating an environment where our employees can thrive both personally and professionally.EEO (Equal Employment Opportunity)RAM Aerospace is an equal opportunity employer. All aspects of employment including the decision to hire, promote, discipline, or discharge, will be based on merit, competence, performance, and business needs. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, marital status, age, national origin, ancestry, physical or mental disability, medical condition, pregnancy, genetic information, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, veteran status, or any other status protected under federal, state, or local law. In addition, it is the policy of RAM Aerospace to provide reasonable accommodation to qualified employees who have protected disabilities to the extent required by applicable laws, regulations, and ordinances where a particular employee works.We welcome former military and law enforcement applicants!

jobs.feedName: Andrew J. Anagnost College of Engineering and Computer Science
jobs.title: Field Engineer Intern at KWH Constructors, Inc.
jobs.description: Employer: KWH Constructors, Inc. Expires: 10/28/2026 Complex Construction and Engineering: Engineering the Complex. Building the Exceptional. Skip the coffee runs – this internship puts you on active jobsites doing the real work of building structural steel projects! KWH Constructors, Inc. is a privately owned, growing steel erector and general contractor with a construction engineering subsidiary (Somerset Construction Engineering). We are looking for a Field Engineer Intern to join our team in the Western United States. KWH is committed to attracting, developing, and retaining the best talent in the industry. KWH offers a competitive salary and benefits, plus the opportunity to help KWH grow into an industry leading contractor in the US. KWH is leading the industry in developing innovative solutions to the most complex construction and engineering challenges where precision, expertise, and vision converge. Our Core Focus is to make the impossible possible – challenging every process, convention, and limitation to deliver extraordinary construction and engineering outcomes for our clients. Incorporated the United States and Canada, KWH is a full service, turn-key construction company specializing in all erection-oriented projects. We are an engineered erector and installer of bridges, machinery, heavy equipment, and complex steel structures. When it comes to the challenging field of structural steel erection, KWH offers superior standards of performance and workmanship by a highly experienced team. From our structural engineers to our construction superintendents and field supervisors, the KWH team knows construction from start to finish. KWH uses innovative methods to complete jobs to the highest standards, in terms of quality, safety, cost efficiency, and value. Reports To: Field Engineer / Project Engineer / Project Manager. Location: Active construction project sites on the West Coast including Alaska (travel may be required). Pay: $25-30/HR, plus housing / travel stipend if applicable Why You’ll Love This Role: Genuinely hands-on — you'll be on active jobsites helping run real production, not just shadowing. Learn industry-leading tools: HeavyJob, Autodesk Forma, and Smartsheet. 1:1 mentorship from Field Engineers, Project Engineers, and Project Managers. A front-row seat to how a structural steel and other projects are built, start to finish. Strong potential path to a full-time Field Engineer I offer after graduation. Competitive pay. What You’ll Do: Help oversee steel erection activities alongside field engineers, project engineers, project managers, and field supervision team. Join daily crew meetings to track the production schedule and confirm materials and equipment are ready. Help review shop drawings, specifications, and project data to support quality and compliance. Support the team in spotting risks to schedule, budget, materials, or process. Complete daily work plans and production planners. Help track production, schedule, and budget performance, and log daily activity in HeavyJob and Autodesk Forma. Support schedule updates in Smartsheet (or other approved tools). Help keep quantity input and cost coding accurate for project financials. Support the Project Manager with status reports and incident documentation as needed. Coordinate with subcontractors, suppliers, engineers, and field supervisors. Support quality control and assurance reviews, inspections, and documentation throughout the project. Help plan and complete field layout alongside crews and engineering. Get exposure to erection plans, submittals, and design drawing development. Help reconcile the closeout checklist with the owner's representative and field crews. Learn what it means to put safety and quality first on every jobsite. As opportunities come up, get exposure to estimating — schedules, quantity takeoffs, and proposal review. What Your Internship Looks Like Onboard (Weeks 1-2): learn the tools (HeavyJob, Forma, Smartsheet, and more), safety protocols, and how a steel erection crew runs day to day. Ongoing: work alongside a Field Engineer on live production tracking, shop drawing review, and field layout — real tasks with real stakes, not busywork. By the end: walk away with a portfolio of real project experience, a mentor network, and — for strong performers — a conversation about a full-time Field Engineer I role. What We’re Looking For: Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering, Construction Engineering, Construction Management, or related field. No construction experience required — prior internship or field exposure is a nice-to-have, not a must. Basic understanding of construction drawings, specifications, or scheduling concepts (coursework counts). Comfortable with Microsoft Office; excited to learn HeavyJob, Autodesk Forma, and Smartsheet. Curious, eager to learn, and not afraid to ask questions on a jobsite. Organized, detail-oriented, and a clear communicator. Open to travel and on-site work at active project locations across the U.S. for the length of the internship. Must be eligible to work in the US. Eligibility to work in Canada would be advantageous. Good to Know: You’ll be on active jobsites – expect time on your feet, uneven terrain, climbing, and all-weather conditions, with PPE always required. Travel to project sites across the Western United States including Alaska may be required, with extended stays as needed. KWH promotes a safe and healthy work environment and provides appropriate safety and equipment training for all personnel as required. Job Type: Full-time (summer), non-exempt. We are an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, national or ethnic origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, disability, protected veteran status or other characteristics protected by law.

jobs.description: Employer: United Water Conservation District Expires: 10/28/2026 Effective January 1, 2027 the Technology Systems Intern salary range will increase from $16.90 - $25.61 per hour to $17.40 - $33.67 per hour. Tier I - $17.40 - $21.15Tier II - $21.70 - $26.39Tier III - $27.70 - $33.67DEFINITIONWorking under the supervision of the Technology Systems Manager, the Technology Systems intern carries out various functions, both technical and administrative, to support the District's computer systems, network, and voice communication equipment and facilities. The intern also assists District staff with related matters. Work is typically conducted during a standard, daytime workweek; however, the role may necessitate occasional evening and weekend work to complete special projects or address urgent requests. The Technology Systems intern is expected to possess a diverse skill set encompassing, but not limited to, Microsoft Windows administration, network security protocols, and basic project management principles. As an integral part of the technology team, the intern will participate in monitoring system performance metrics, assist in procedural documentation, and collaborate closely with both District control systems staff and senior technology personnel. This role will offer the intern a comprehensive experience in enterprise-level information technology practices, and provide opportunities for implementing solutions that align with federal, state, and industry-specific regulations. In summary, the Technology Systems intern will be a vital asset to the Technology Systems team, supporting a broad array of initiatives and ensuring that the District's technology infrastructure operates efficiently and securely. The position serves as a foundational role for those aspiring to further their career in information technology, offering a rich tapestry of tasks that touch upon system administration, policy formulation, and end-user support. This includes aiding in the maintenance of records for all licenses, warranty information, and schedules for equipment replacement, as well as contributing to the upkeep of service and support agreements.Conduct quality assurance by administering tests on newly introduced software, hardware, or configurations prior to full-scale implementation. Thoroughly document the test results, including any issues encountered, and provide comprehensive reports for review.In collaboration with District control systems staff, senior technology systems personnel, and network administrators, provide support for the administration and management of the District's Wide Area Network, Local Area Network, broadband services, and District internet circuits, implementing requisite modifications as circumstances dictate.Aid in the development and delivery of educational materials and sessions aimed at bolstering the technological proficiency of District staff, encompassing workshops, tutorials, and written guides.Participate in meetings and communications with technology vendors, assisting in the assessment and qualification of products or services, as well as coordinating the procurement process, including order placements, delivery tracking, and verification of contract compliance.Conduct research to identify new technologies, hardware upgrades, and software updates that could benefit the District, then summarize these findings into reports for review by management.Support senior staff in managing technology-related projects, from the initial stages of scoping and planning to execution and closeout, utilizing project management software as required. Directory, Azure active directory, and cloud-based services.Remote access fundamentals and VPNs, mobile access.Microsoft SQL server, database administration.Software and hardware licensing and support principles.Asset lifestyle and management.System management and patch management fundamentals.General business principles, including developing basic budgets and tracking expenses.Operations control systems (ICS/SCADA), preferred.Fundamental information security systems best practices.Identity management, multi-factor authentication, and single sign-on fundamentals.Anti-virus, Anti-malware, behavioral guard, threat prevention principles.DevOps fundamentals with Azure cloud-based services, Amazon Web Services (AWS), and Google Cloud (GCloud).Fundamentals of IT Service Management.Basic Scripting and Automation capabilities.Documentation skills aligned with industry best practices.Collaboration tools such as Microsoft Teams.Soft skills including communication, problem-solving, and teamwork.Ethical considerations in IT.Regulatory compliance relevant to U.S. critical infrastructure.Customer service principles.Change management best practices.Project timeline awareness.Ability to:Manage and complete multiple, varied assignments within prescribed deadlines despite frequent interruptions.Adapt to, learn, and support new technologies and software applications in alignment with organizational needs.Liaise effectively with internal departments, external organizations, District staff, and vendors for problem-solving, knowledge-sharing, and policy implementation.Communicate effectively, both orally and in writing, including the development and administration of IT policies, procedures, and training materials.Read and interpret technical instructions, safety rules, operating guidelines, and procedure manuals.Maintain confidentiality and exercise discretion when handling sensitive or proprietary information.Analyze, track, and recommend solutions for technology issues, employing an effective course of action.Prioritize tasks, manage time effectively, and adhere to strict deadlines for system maintenance and issue resolution.Assist departmental staff in evaluating options for potential technology applications and systems.Perform minor hardware repairs and coordinate with support vendors for software and hardware issues.Track, administer, and organize a variety of hardware, software, licenses, and support agreements.Document expenses accurately and adhere to prescribed budgets.Respond to and identify user network and computer-related problems. EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCEExperience providing IT support in a business environment is required. Some of this experience may have been gained education pursued towards a Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a comparable field is preferred but not required.CERTIFICATIONS AND LICENSESPossession of a valid California Class C Driver’s License is required upon hire.
